page: Vultr vbm-64c-1536gb-amd is a bare metal server within the Bare Metal NVMe family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9354 processor containing 64 physical cores and 128 threads with a dedicated allocation running at 3.2 GHz. The system is configured with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, which yields 12.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a single 480 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No graphics processing unit is included in this configuration.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates top-tier capabilities, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU performance with a stress-ng multi-core score of 203240.04 and a PassMark CPU score of 117661.25. Memory performance is similarly positioned in the top 10%, with a read-only small block bandwidth of 10045.41 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 329.05 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, with the system processing 170.67 million Redis SET operations per second. For language model workloads, the server achieves 288.98 tokens per second for prompt processing and 41.85 tokens per second for text generation using a medium 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of this server configuration is the modest 480 GB local NVMe SSD, which is small relative to the massive 1.5 TB memory capacity and 128 vCPUs. This makes the server highly cost-efficient for memory-bound, compute-heavy workloads that do not require extensive local storage, while workloads with massive storage requirements may require external storage integration. This hardware profile is suited for in-memory databases, virtualization hypervisors, multi-threaded scientific computing, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
description: Vultr vbm-64c-1536gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring an AMD EPYC 9354 processor with 64 physical cores, 128 vCPUs, and a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core, and a 480 GB NVMe SSD. Lacking a GPU, this server relies on its massive memory capacity and compute density. Benchmark results place its multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations in the top 10% tier, with Redis SET operations reaching 170.67 million operations per second. While the 480 GB local storage is modest relative to the system's compute and memory resources, the server is highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads. It is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale virtualization, and heavy multi-threaded data processing.
